currentContext.strengths: U2O (Unorganised-to-Organised) distribution: deep distribution network and targeted product offerings enabling penetration across semi-urban and rural markets|Strong omni-channel execution across offline retail, e-commerce and emerging formats; added 600 net new showrooms in FY26|Integrated multi-brand leadership across price points (Sleepwell, Kurlon), enhanced by successful integration of the Kurlon business enabling deeper market penetration and channel productivity|Technology-led operational enablement via digital arm Staqo - analytics, process automation and decision-support systems|Diversified and improving international business across Australia, Spain and the GCC region, supported by tighter cost management and pricing discipline|Multi-channel distribution network of over 11,000+ touch points; ~30% share of the Indian branded mattress segment and ~40% share in Australia
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen customer engagement, advance innovation and enhance operational excellence across the business|Continue to expand market reach through a deeper physical retail network, including COCO stores, while further strengthening presence across e-commerce platforms with a sharper focus on the own brand.com channel|Pursue growth in select adjacent categories, including premium and luxury mattresses and foam-led solutions|Strengthen raw material capabilities to improve supply resilience and reduce exposure to external volatility|Deepen the U2O (Unorganised-to-Organised) distribution initiative across semi-urban and rural markets for long-term demand creation|Strengthen omni-channel coordination through investments in backend systems, demand visibility and channel coordination|Furlenco to continue scaling its footprint, leveraging omni-channel integration opportunities within the Group and the SFL/KEL retail networks|Staqo to continue building scale and profitability through the Presence360 unified enterprise digital platform|Execution centred on integration stability, cost discipline and profitable growth across categories and geographies|Advance the Sustainability 2030 roadmap - renewable energy, water stewardship and resource-efficiency initiatives|In Australia and Spain, pursue focused operational interventions - cost optimisation, sourcing efficiencies, tighter overhead control and yield/process optimisation to drive manufacturing consistency|For FY26 the Board recommended, and shareholders are to consider and declare at the 54th AGM, a final dividend of Re. 1 (20%) per equity share of face value Rs 5/- each. The Company also re-appointed its statutory auditors (M S K A & Associates LLP) for a second five-year term (FY2026-27 to FY2030-31), consistent with a governance framework emphasising Board oversight of annual operating/capital budgets, quarterly review of financial performance, and disclosure discipline around material transactions, investments and related-party dealings.
currentContext.expansion: Growth-related capacity/footprint narrative in FY26 centred on the B2B (technical foam) business and the core mattress/foam distribution network rather than a named new-plant project. In B2B, the Company strengthened its presence in high-performance applications - automotive comfort systems, NVH (Noise, Vibration, Harshness) solutions and certified foams for railways and aerospace - and progressed import substitution, commercialising indigenously developed products to reduce reliance on imports. Operational focus remained on optimising capacity utilisation, improving manufacturing efficiencies and investing in R&D/technical capabilities for faster product development. Internationally, focused operational interventions in Australia and Spain (cost optimisation, sourcing efficiencies, tighter overhead control, yield optimisation, scrap-recovery and waste-monetisation, advanced foaming technologies, structured plant-level monitoring) strengthened manufacturing consistency across facilities globally. The Company crossed a milestone of over 100,000 MT of foam production globally (India, Australia and Spain) in FY 2025-26, its highest annual foam production. On distribution/retail footprint, the Company added showrooms and expanded COCO (company-owned company-operated) stores, expanded its U2O dealer network to 8,400+ dealers across 24+ states and 5,500+ towns, and continues to scale its GCC-region presence through e-commerce, retail expansion and local partnerships.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic sensitivity of demand and input costs
risks.note: Management flags that inflation, interest-rate movements and economic slowdown may impact consumer demand and input costs, given the company's exposure to discretionary consumer spending on mattresses and comfort products.

risks.risk: Raw material availability and supply chain disruption
risks.note: Fluctuations in raw material availability and supply chain disruptions can affect production efficiency and product quality; the Company relies on strategic sourcing, bulk procurement and supplier diversification to manage this.
Inventory management is flagged as critical, as excess stock could lead to higher carrying costs and potential obsolescence.

risks.risk: Intense competition from organised and unorganised players
risks.note: The industry continues to witness intense competition from both organised and unorganised players, exerting pressure on pricing and margins.

Evolving regulatory requirements and the presence of counterfeit products pose risks to compliance and brand integrity, addressed via robust quality processes, product authentication measures and market surveillance.

risks.risk: Shifting consumer preferences and channel disruption
risks.note: Changing consumer preferences towards innovative, sustainable and digitally enabled products, along with a growing shift towards online purchasing, are reshaping demand patterns and require continued digital/omni-channel investment to stay aligned.

risks.risk: Geopolitical tensions and crude-oil price volatility
risks.note: Global uncertainties, including geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions, and volatility in crude oil prices (a key PU-foam feedstock driver), are flagged as key risks introducing input-cost uncertainty, longer transit times and elevated freight costs.

Global trade growth is projected to moderate, reflecting evolving tariff structures and increasing protectionist policies, which management flags as a source of uneven growth and cautious business sentiment across regions the Company operates in (India, Australia, Spain, GCC).

one-line thesis: Sheela Foam delivered record FY26 profitability (PAT up 78% YoY) driven by successful Kurlon integration and volume-led operating leverage, validating the shift from growth-at-all-costs to profitable scale. The first-ever dividend declaration and rapid debt reduction signal a mature capital allocation phase, while U2O and e-commerce channels provide structural growth runways despite elevated raw material costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,050cr (Q4, +24% YoY), INR 3,821cr (FY26, +11% YoY); EBITDA: INR 121cr (Q4, +90% YoY), Margin 11.5% (+400bps YoY); PAT: INR 92cr (Q4, 7x YoY), INR 161cr (FY26, +78% YoY) - Note: INR 144cr of FY26 PAT generated in H2 due to H1 mark-to-market losses on govt securities; Order Book: N/A (B2C/B2B mix); Net Debt: Reduced by INR 156cr in FY26, consolidated debt ~INR 600-700cr.
guidance: Revenue Growth: >15% volume growth targeted for FY27; Margin: Core EBITDA margin trajectory >11-12% bracket; Order Inflow: U2O and E-commerce prioritized for penetration; Capex: INR 125-150cr for FY27 (maintenance + debottlenecking + new stores).
order book & pipeline: Not applicable for B2C/B2B model; Demand visibility driven by 600 net new showrooms added in FY26 and 8,400 U2O dealers.
segment / subsidiary detail: Mattress: Vol +13% (Q4), Value +13% (Q4); Foam: Vol +34% (Q4), Value +36% (Q4); U2O: Vol +65%, Value +111% (FY26) driven by higher ASP models; E-commerce: Brand.com +136%, Platforms +39% (FY26); International: Australia Rev INR 422cr (EBITDA 10%), Spain Rev INR 391cr (EBITDA 10.4%).
growth verticals / optionality: Pillow category monetization (previously freebie); Furlenco scaling to INR 500cr (FY27) with potential IPO in 12-15 months; U2O expansion into deeper tier-3/4 towns; Staqo digital arm monetization.
margins & cost dynamics: Core EBITDA margin 11.5% (Q4) vs 7.5% (Q4FY25); Raw materials (TDI/Polyol) up 25-35% YoY but largely passed through; Price hikes implemented across B2C/B2B/Industrial; Inventory turnover (~10-15 days) mitigates lag effects; Depreciation guidance INR 140-145cr for FY27 following policy realignment to match asset useful life (40-50 yrs).
capex / expansion: FY27 guidance INR 125-150cr inclusive of maintenance, debottlenecking, and marketing capex (new stores); 500kW solar operational at Jabalpur, 1MW+ pipeline across other units.
capital allocation: First-ever dividend recommended (20%); Net debt reduction of INR 156cr in FY26; India debt (~INR 300cr) target repayment in 1-1.5 years via operating cash flows; International debt (~INR 350cr) self-liquidating from local cash flows; Furlenco stake (43%) held for valuation uplift via future IPO.
risks & watch-items: Raw material volatility (TDI/Polyol prices oscillating INR 180-220/kg); Geopolitical tension in Middle East impacting supply chains; Integration execution risks in international subsidiaries; Competitive intensity in unorganized segment.
management quality / tone: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' over sheer scale; Transparent on RM volatility but assured of pass-through capability; Strategic patience on Furlenco IPO and international divestment opportunities.
non-obvious takeaways: Depreciation policy changed to align with 40-50 year asset life (from aggressive WDV), reducing front-loaded expense skew; U2O value growth (111%) outpacing volume (65%) indicates successful mix-shift to higher ASP models, not just volume push; Furlenco ROCE at 30-35% significantly exceeds parent's ~18%, hidden value driver.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility squeezing smaller unorganized players unable to hedge or pass on costs. | Sheela Foam Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management confirmed market share gains in Q4 as smaller competitors failed to supply during RM spikes; integrated supply chain ensures continuity. |
| Furlenco's path to profitability and scale required capital and operational discipline. | Furlenco (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | PAT surged to INR 60cr from INR 3cr; Sheela Foam's 43% stake offers significant optionality upon planned IPO. |
| European margin compression due to energy costs and demand slowdown. | European Competitors | loser | Low | Sheela's Spain/Australia ops improved margins to ~10% via restructuring, suggesting peers without similar efficiency programs may lose share. |

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

hero.oneLiner: Sheela Foam Limited is one of India's leading integrated comfort-solutions companies, manufacturing polyurethane foam and mattresses under the Sleepwell and Kurlon brands, with international operations in Australia and Spain.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Sheela Foam Limited is one of India's leading integrated comfort-solutions companies, manufacturing polyurethane foam and mattresses under the Sleepwell and Kurlon brands, with international operations in Australia and Spain.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Incorporated in 1971, Sheela Foam operates a fully integrated business model spanning PU foam manufacturing, product design, branding, distribution and digital engagement, serving mattress, comfort foam, technical foam and furniture-cushioning segments for both consumer and industrial customers (automotive, furniture, packaging, infrastructure). Its flagship brands Sleepwell and Kurlon lead the Indian mattress industry, complemented by adjacent platforms Furlenco (furniture rental/digital-first) and Staqo (technology and data arm), alongside international operations in Australia, Spain and the GCC region.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable for B2C/B2B model; Demand visibility driven by 600 net new showrooms added in FY26 and 8,400 U2O dealers.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: >15% volume growth targeted for FY27; Margin: Core EBITDA margin trajectory >11-12% bracket; Order Inflow: U2O and E-commerce prioritized for penetration; Capex: INR 125-150cr for FY27 (maintenance + debottlenecking + new stores).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Pillow category monetization (previously freebie); Furlenco scaling to INR 500cr (FY27) with potential IPO in 12-15 months; U2O expansion into deeper tier-3/4 towns; Staqo digital arm monetization.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India expected to remain the fastest-growing major economy, with growth supported by continued government capital expenditure and a recovery in private consumption
- The Indian mattress industry is at an inflection point, transitioning from an unorganised, price-led structure towards a more organised and branded ecosystem with rising preference for quality, durability and standardised products
- Growth drivers cited for the mattress industry: rising disposable incomes and lifestyle upgradation, growing health and sleep awareness, shift towards branded and premium products, favourable demographics, product innovation (memory foam, hybrid, technology-enabled), and e-commerce/D2C expansion
- Opportunities cited: expanding consumer base into tier II/III cities, shift towards sleep wellness, organised retail expansion, institutional demand growth from real estate/hospitality/healthcare construction activity, sustainability-led innovation, and digital/e-commerce penetration
- Indian mattress industry outlook expected to sustain growth supported by continued premiumisation, increasing formalisation and expanding digital adoption, with improving product mix and deeper market penetration
- Australia's economy expected to see GDP growth moderate from 2.3% (CY2025) to 1.8% (CY2026) with easing inflation and resilient domestic demand supporting the local business
- Spain's economy expected to moderate to ~2.2% growth in CY2026 with resilient domestic demand, though export momentum is expected to soften
- Global macro risks flagged as demand-relevant: geopolitical tensions in the Middle East/Strait of Hormuz disrupting shipping routes and elevating freight costs, plus crude-oil price volatility introducing input-cost uncertainty
- Global trade growth projected to moderate due to evolving tariff structures and increasing protectionist policies, weighing on business sentiment

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Core EBITDA margin 11.5% (Q4) vs 7.5% (Q4FY25); Raw materials (TDI/Polyol) up 25-35% YoY but largely passed through; Price hikes implemented across B2C/B2B/Industrial; Inventory turnover (~10-15 days) mitigates lag effects; Depreciation guidance INR 140-145cr for FY27 following policy realignment to match asset useful life (40-50 yrs).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: First-ever dividend recommended (20%); Net debt reduction of INR 156cr in FY26; India debt (~INR 300cr) target repayment in 1-1.5 years via operating cash flows; International debt (~INR 350cr) self-liquidating from local cash flows; Furlenco stake (43%) held for valuation uplift via future IPO.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Growth-related capacity/footprint narrative in FY26 centred on the B2B (technical foam) business and the core mattress/foam distribution network rather than a named new-plant project. In B2B, the Company strengthened its presence in high-performance applications - automotive comfort systems, NVH (Noise, Vibration, Harshness) solutions and certified foams for railways and aerospace - and progressed import substitution, commercialising indigenously developed products to reduce reliance on imports. Operational focus remained on optimising capacity utilisation, improving manufacturing efficiencies and investing in R&D/technical capabilities for faster product development. Internationally, focused operational interventions in Australia and Spain (cost optimisation, sourcing efficiencies, tighter overhead control, yield optimisation, scrap-recovery and waste-monetisation, advanced foaming technologies, structured plant-level monitoring) strengthened manufacturing consistency across facilities globally. The Company crossed a milestone of over 100,000 MT of foam production globally (India, Australia and Spain) in FY 2025-26, its highest annual foam production. On distribution/retail footprint, the Company added showrooms and expanded COCO (company-owned company-operated) stores, expanded its U2O dealer network to 8,400+ dealers across 24+ states and 5,500+ towns, and continues to scale its GCC-region presence through e-commerce, retail expansion and local partnerships.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and execution-focused; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' over sheer scale; Transparent on RM volatility but assured of pass-through capability; Strategic patience on Furlenco IPO and international divestment opportunities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- U2O (Unorganised-to-Organised) distribution: deep distribution network and targeted product offerings enabling penetration across semi-urban and rural markets
- Strong omni-channel execution across offline retail, e-commerce and emerging formats; added 600 net new showrooms in FY26
- Integrated multi-brand leadership across price points (Sleepwell, Kurlon), enhanced by successful integration of the Kurlon business enabling deeper market penetration and channel productivity
- Technology-led operational enablement via digital arm Staqo - analytics, process automation and decision-support systems
- Diversified and improving international business across Australia, Spain and the GCC region, supported by tighter cost management and pricing discipline
- Multi-channel distribution network of over 11,000+ touch points; ~30% share of the Indian branded mattress segment and ~40% share in Australia

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material volatility (TDI/Polyol prices oscillating INR 180-220/kg); Geopolitical tension in Middle East impacting supply chains; Integration execution risks in international subsidiaries; Competitive intensity in unorganized segment.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Depreciation policy changed to align with 40-50 year asset life (from aggressive WDV), reducing front-loaded expense skew; U2O value growth (111%) outpacing volume (65%) indicates successful mix-shift to higher ASP models, not just volume push; Furlenco ROCE at 30-35% significantly exceeds parent's ~18%, hidden value driver.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen customer engagement, advance innovation and enhance operational excellence across the business
- Continue to expand market reach through a deeper physical retail network, including COCO stores, while further strengthening presence across e-commerce platforms with a sharper focus on the own brand.com channel
- Pursue growth in select adjacent categories, including premium and luxury mattresses and foam-led solutions
- Strengthen raw material capabilities to improve supply resilience and reduce exposure to external volatility
- Deepen the U2O (Unorganised-to-Organised) distribution …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material price volatility squeezing smaller unorganized players unable to hedge or pass on costs. | Sheela Foam Ltd | beneficiary | High | Management confirmed market share gains in Q4 as smaller competitors failed to supply during RM spikes; integrated supply chain ensures continuity. |
| Furlenco's path to profitability and scale required capital and operational discipline. | Furlenco (Unlisted) | beneficiary | Med | PAT surged to INR 60cr from INR 3cr; Sheela Foam's 43% stake offers significant optionality upon planned IPO. |
| European margin compression due to energy costs and demand slowdown. | European Competitors | loser | Low | Sheela's Spain/Australia ops improved margins to ~10% via restructuring, suggesting peers without similar efficiency programs may lose share. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [E-commerce] Q1 FY27 e-commerce is called out as the volume driver, with 19% YoY sales growth on platforms and 69% YoY sales growth on brand.com.
- [Milestone] The deck flags "1ST TIME EVER in Q1" crossing Rs 1000 Cr+ revenue and Rs 100 Cr+ EBITDA (consolidated basis).
- [U2O] A slide titled "Q1 FY27 | Strengthening U2O outreach" carries the counts 24+, 9900+, 230+ and 5500+, but the labels for these four numbers are lost in extraction, so none of them can be attributed to a metric.
- [CSR reporting gap] The CSR initiative slides show the column headings (Key Objective, FY26 Achievements, Q1FY27 Achievements) with the cells rendering only as "In actions", so no CSR outcome figures are stated.
